solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stupid fling — man plainly left out the need for this

definitions.text: Stupid fling — man plainly left out the need for this

indicators.note: a stupid arrangement is a senseless one, so the letters of the following words are muddled
the letter for left is put out of the word plainly before the mix

explanation.surface: A man's foolish affair, carried on without precaution, leads to an unplanned outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' gives L and 'out' drops it from PLAINLY; the rest of FLING MAN PLAINLY is shuffled by 'Stupid'. The whole clue then describes what the careless lover lacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraception, the practice of controlling when children arrive, is what a careless fling with no precautions needs.

clue.text: Person online abusing female gets disabled, right?

parts.note: lame means disabled, unable to walk properly

explanation.surface: An internet troll picks on a disabled woman, and the clue asks if that is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who posts hostile, insulting messages in internet forums is said to be flaming them.

clue.text: Cooked one third of shanks (of lamb) for group formed online

indicators.note: cooked suggests something prepared and altered, so the letters are rearranged
a third of the six letters of shanks is its first two

explanation.surface: A recipe note: lamb shanks partly cooked, oddly attributed to an internet group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one third of' takes SH, the first two of the six letters of 'shanks'; 'Cooked' rearranges SH with OF LAMB.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of crowd is organised through social media to gather suddenly in a public place and perform.

clue.text: Catch crabs, say, with this primarily sexual sort of a night in unreliable setting

indicators.note: in tells us the following letters go inside the word for unreliable
the unreliable word acts as a setting, holding the other letters like a jewel

parts.note: fickle means changeable, not to be relied on

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the opening letter of sexual
a sort of something is a variation on it, so the letters of a night are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smutty innuendo about catching crabs after a night with a fickle partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges A NIGHT, and 'in' with 'setting' treats the unreliable word as a mount holding the letters, as a ring holds a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Rods, lines, hooks and nets are the gear used to catch crabs and other creatures from the water.

clue.text: Tom is one following row on Twitter?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
E, short for electronic, marks something done online, as on Twitter
a line is a row of things

explanation.surface: Someone named Tom is a follower caught up in a social media spat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like an argument, but it is a line, a row in the sense of a straight series.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom is a male cat, and cats belong to the cat family, so a tom is one of these.

clue.text: Fellow nearest broken window

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

indicators.note: broken means smashed into a different arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man standing close by has smashed a window.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an anatomical term, from Latin, for a small opening in bone, such as those in the inner ear.

clue.text: Thus everyone gets to feel musical regularly, praise the Lord!

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of feel musical is taken

explanation.surface: A joyous congregation all feel musical and break into worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th letters and so on of 'feel musical': ELUIA.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hebrew exclamation used in hymns and worship literally means praise ye the Lord.

clue.text: Acoustic effect in long note recorded backwards by Queen?

indicators.note: by means next to, so the queen's letter sits beside the next piece

parts.note: R, for regina, is the abbreviation for queen

indicators.note: something recorded backwards plays in reverse, so the word for the long note is turned round

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note, worth two semibreves

explanation.surface: A sound engineer discusses a long note played backwards on a Queen record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks like the rock band, but it is R; 'recorded backwards' turns BREVE into EVERB.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for reverberation, this is the echoing effect added to recordings to make them sound fuller.

clue.text: Where one number appears in a decimal fraction is irrelevant

definitions.text: Where one number appears in a decimal fraction
definitions.meaning: digits after the decimal point sit to its side, literally next to the point
not pertinent to the matter being discussed

explanation.walkthrough: In 0.5, the five appears right next to the decimal point.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a remark that does not bear on the matter at hand, not touching its central issue.

clue.text: The Pope misinterpreted Acts 5? Horrific!

indicators.note: something misinterpreted is read the wrong way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the words are taken as written, except the figure five, which becomes the Roman numeral V

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled at a pontiff's reading of a chapter of the Acts of the Apostles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acts 5' reads as a Bible reference, but it gives ACTS plus V to mix with HORRIFIC.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional title of the Pope, as Christ's representative on earth in Catholic teaching.

clue.text: One little creature's lacking head and feet

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: lacking its head means losing the first letter

parts.note: a lamb is a little creature, and the 's is read as plural

explanation.surface: A small animal has no head and no feet, a grisly picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feet' looks like part of the creature but is the definition, metrical feet in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry a foot is a unit of rhythm, and these feet each have a short syllable then a long one.

clue.text: Perilous state of child's walking reins, perhaps, currently broken in two places

indicators.note: broken means split open, so the harness word is cut to take a letter
the harness word is opened at two different points, each taking a letter

parts.note: walking reins for a toddler are an example of a harness
I is the physics symbol for electric current
the current symbol again, used a second time

explanation.surface: A toddler's safety harness is worn out in two spots, which makes things dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currently' supplies I (the symbol for current) twice, once for each break: HA-I-R-I-NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something hairy is dangerous or frightening, so this noun names a risky, scary condition.

clue.text: Story about Madoff's gardener in New York

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the story word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a yarn is a story, often a tall one
the name splits as mad plus off, and off signals the three letters of mad are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tale about the fraudster Bernie Madoff's gardener, set in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madoff's' reads as the jailed financier's name, but split as 'mad off' it is MAD scrambled ('off' as in gone wrong).
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a yard is a garden, so the man who tends it is a gardener.

clue.text: Given tip-off tenor's drunk beer and wine? On the contrary

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: drinking something takes it inside, so one piece goes into another
this reverses the surface, so the wine takes in the tenor, not the tenor the wine

parts.note: red is a colour of wine
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A tipsy tenor has downed beer and wine before getting a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has the tenor drinking the wine; 'On the contrary' flips it so the wine holds the tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been tipped off has been warned in advance and so made watchful.

clue.text: Finally, and yet significantly, there's a lack of energy!

definitions.meaning: an idiom for a final item that still matters
the word for least, written without its E for energy, becomes the word for final

explanation.surface: A tired speaker concludes by admitting a shortage of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: LEAST with no E (energy) is LAST, so last is least but not E.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces the final item in a list while insisting it matters just as much as the rest.

clue.text: County cricket season broadcast starting sooner each time

indicators.note: broadcast means put on air, so a word is given as it sounds

parts.note: summer is when cricket is played in England

indicators.note: starting means the beginning letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: A cricket season's coverage begins earlier every year.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMERSET is a county in south-west England with a first-class cricket side; 'broadcast' gives SOMER for summer, and 'starting' takes SET from sooner each time.
explanation.definitionFit: This south-western English administrative region is one of the historic shires of England.

clue.text: Wish to play cricket, when "empty" vessel

parts.note: to long is to wish

indicators.note: when here signals one piece taken inside another

parts.note: to bat is to play cricket, taking the strike
O, a zero, stands for nothing, so for empty

explanation.surface: Someone longs to play cricket, and the clue wonders about an empty boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' gives O, a nought meaning nothing, the letter shaped like an empty ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A Viking-style ship or the largest boat carried by a sailing ship is a vessel of this name.

clue.text: Greek character has crime somehow figured out?

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters of crime are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shady Greek has had his crime worked out, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figured out' reads as solved, but it means set out in figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Data expressed in figures, as numbers rather than words, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Be sorry some winter germs turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters read from bottom to top
some means a part of, so a stretch of letters is taken from inside winter germs

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for the germs that appeared in winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes TERGER from wintER GERms, and 'turned up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel sorrow or remorse about something you did is to wish it undone.

clue.text: Do well to shut up

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them, to con them
fine means well, in good health

explanation.surface: Advice that the way to succeed is to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut up' looks like be quiet, but it means imprison.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock someone in or keep them within limits is to imprison them.

clue.text: Maintain relative has no hesitation following One Direction

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the relative piece is placed after the others

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
N, for north, is a compass direction

indicators.note: has no means a piece is taken away from the relative word

parts.note: a sister is a relative
er is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: A boy-band fan's sister confidently backs One Direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One Direction' looks like the boy band but gives I and N; SISTER loses ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to maintain or assert something firmly despite objection.

clue.text: Soldier in Irish uniform

parts.note: regular means uniform, the same throughout

explanation.surface: A soldier is wearing Irish army uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like a soldier's dress, but it is an adjective meaning even.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter in a guerrilla band or other force outside a regular army is called this.

clue.text: Go over for wrestling tournament

parts.note: a go or a bash is an attempt
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone is told to head over to a wrestling contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go over' reads as travel to; it is BASH (have a go) plus O. A basho is a Japanese sumo tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: In Japanese sumo, each of the official championships held through the year is known by this word.

clue.text: Cove with hot spring, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a geyser is a spring that spouts hot water

explanation.surface: A coastal inlet with a hot spring, perhaps in Iceland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cove' looks like a bay, but it is old British slang for a man, as is GEEZER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a man or fellow, a bloke.

clue.text: Like a special regiment confronting evil killer

parts.note: as means like
the SAS, the Special Air Service, is a British special forces regiment
sin is evil, wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A special forces unit faces an evil murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer, especially one who kills a prominent person for political or paid reasons.
